messages:
maya: quick heads-up — eu-west p99 spiked after the routing tweak last deploy. baseline ~180ms -> 720ms for ~10m window. p95 barely moved. anyone seeing this?

ops-bot: alert: service=inference-runtime region=eu-west severity=warning p99=720ms window=10m deploy=canary-routing-2026-03-17

jerome: which model/route? can you paste route id + sample trace? dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/route/rt-493

maya: route=chat-gen-v2, mostly short sequences <=512 but some bursts of longer history. attaching quick notes from traces below.

sahil: quick profiling notes from the 5m capture during the spike:
- KV cache global hit-rate dropped 98.6% -> 82.1% (correlated with cross-region fallbacks)
- microbatching window = 8ms; queue depth variance increased and we saw occasional 30ms wait spikes
- kernel_selector fell back to generic kernel for shards when seq > ~800 due to padding/shape path regression in last runtime build (commit a1b2c3)
- no obvious CUDA OOMs or GC pauses

=> hypothesis: cross-region fallback caused cold KV misses which triggered extra prep + kernel fallback path; that combo creates a heavy tail for p99 while p95 stays stable

li: flame snapshot (top entries):
```
trace 0x7f...
50% time: kv::lookup
20% time: runtime::dispatch_generic_kernel
12% time: batch::wait_queue
8% time: cudnn_gemm_slow_path
```

jerome: if KV miss is the main driver, why do we see p95 so stable?

sahil: because cached traffic (the vast majority) uses fast kernel and cached KV entries. p99 is dominated by rare chains: miss -> extra preprocessing -> kernel fallback/slow kernel -> queue backpressure -> next requests pile up. it's multiplicative

maya: mitigation ideas (short-term):
- revert routing tweak to prefer eu-west-local for chat-gen-v2 (fast rollback)
- disable cross-region fallback for this route temporarily
- consider increasing microbatch window to 12ms (reduces overhead but raises avg latency)
- force kernel_selector policy to prefer compiled kernels for seq ranges we hit

jerome: I can push a patch to routing policy (canary revert) now. also recommend sticky-session affinity to keep KV locality

li: rolled canary revert on a subset of hosts -> quick observation: p99 dropped to ~230ms in canary after 5m. KV hit-rate recovered.

perfbot: canary-report: route=chat-gen-v2 region=eu-west p99_before=720ms p99_after=230ms kv_hit_before=82.1% kv_hit_after=97.9% microbatch_mean=8.2ms -> 8.0ms

sahil: follow-ups to track:
- add regression test for kernel-selector padding thresholds (boundaries: 512 / 768 / 1024)
- Emit a chained-event metric: cache-miss -> kernel-fallback -> queue-delay so we can alert on correlated spikes
- perf lab sweep for microbatch/window: test windows [4,8,12,20]ms and measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec tradeoffs

maya: agree. created INF-849 to track the action items and test plan. canary revert left in place until we validate. thanks all :thumbsup:
